paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, huai lai a Israel gam a kumpipa a-om louh lai in, Levi chi a mi khat Ephraim tanggam tawp lam ah a-om a, Judah gam a Bethlehem mi mei in anei hi.
heading: Levi mi Leh Amei
english: In those days, when there was no king in Israel, there was a certain Levite living on the farther side of the hill country of Ephraim, who took for himself a concubine out of Bethlehem Judah.

paite: Amei in ang a kawm san a, huchi in Judah gam a Bethlehem a apa inn ah ataisan hi. Huai ah kha li tak a-om hi.
english: His concubine played the prostitute against him, and went away from him to her father’s house to Bethlehem Judah, and was there for four months.

paite: Apasal athou a, asikha leh asabiltung nih pi in kamdam in ava khem a, lungkim a pikik nawn tum in ava delhzui hi. Ama'n apa inn ah ana pilut a, apa'n ana muh in ana kipahpih hi.
english: Her husband arose and went after her to speak kindly to her, to bring her again, having his servant with him and a couple of donkeys. She brought him into her father’s house; and when the father of the young lady saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.

paite: Asungpa, numei pa'n akiang a om ding in ana khou a; akiang ah ni thum a-om a, ane un adawnkhawm ua, huai ah atung hi.
english: His father-in-law, the young lady’s father, kept him there; and he stayed with him three days. So they ate and drank, and stayed there.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, ani li ni in zingkhang in athou a, amah bel pawt tum in athou hi. Numei pa'n amakpa kiang ah, "Tanghou tawmchik ne in. Na lungtang hihhalh tadih inla, huai khit chiang in na pai na ding," achi hi.
english: On the fourth day, they got up early in the morning, and he rose up to depart. The young lady’s father said to his son-in-law, “Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward you shall go your way.”

paite: Huchi in atu ua, anih un ane un adawnkhawm uh. Numei pa'n huai mi kiang ah, "Lungkimtak in tuzan giak in, na lungtang nuamsak in," achi hi.
english: So they sat down, ate, and drank, both of them together. Then the young lady’s father said to the man, “Please be pleased to stay all night, and let your heart be merry.”

paite: Huai mi bel pawt tum in athou a, himahleh asungpa'n azolzol a, agiak nawnta hi.
english: The man rose up to depart; but his father-in-law urged him, and he stayed there again.

paite: Ani nga zingkhangpi in pawt tum in athou hi. Numei pa'n, "Na lungtang hihhalh tadih lechin akei dia, nitak ninem hun tan bek om tadih in," achi hi. Huchi in anih un an anekhawm nawn uhi.
english: He arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart; and the young lady’s father said, “Please strengthen your heart and stay until the day declines;” and they both ate.

paite: Huai mi bel amei leh asikha toh pawt tum a akisakleh asungpa, numei pa'n akiang ah, "Ngai in, ni leng akaita, tuzan giak nawn mai inla, ni leng tum ding ahita. Hiai ah giak in; na lungtang akipahna ding in. Huchi in zingchiang in zingkhang in na thou dia, inn lam ah na pai mai ding," achi hi.
english: When the man rose up to depart, he, and his concubine, and his servant, his father-in-law, the young lady’s father, said to him, “Behold, now the day draws toward evening, please stay all night. Behold, the day is ending. Stay here, that your heart may be merry; and tomorrow go on your way early, that you may go home.”

paite: Himahleh huai mi huai zan giah a-ut kei a, athou a, apawtta hi. Jebus kho zawn atung a, huai tuh Jerusalem khua ahi, sabiltung nih bawlsa api a; amei leng atel hi.
english: But the man wouldn’t stay that night, but he rose up and went near Jebus (also called Jerusalem). With him were a couple of saddled donkeys. His concubine also was with him.

paite: Jebus kho kiang atun un ni akai mahmahta hi. Sikha in apu kiang ah, "Hong pai dih, hiai Jebuste khopi ah i lut mai dia, i giak mai ding," achi hi.
english: When they were by Jebus, the day was far spent; and the servant said to his master, “Please come and let’s enter into this city of the Jebusites, and stay in it.”

paite: Apu'n akiang ah, "Israel suan hilou namdang khua ah lut lou e. Gibeah kholam i zuan zaw ding," achi hi.
english: His master said to him, “We won’t enter into the city of a foreigner that is not of the children of Israel; but we will pass over to Gibeah.”

paite: Asikha kiang ah, "Kisa aw, hiai munte akoi zaw hiam i zuan ding. Gibeah ah hiam, Ramah ah hiam i giak ding," achi hi.
english: He said to his servant, “Come and let’s draw near to one of these places; and we will lodge in Gibeah, or in Ramah.”

paite: Huchi in apai nawn zel ua; Benjaminte Gibeah kho kiang atun un ni atumta hi.
english: So they passed on and went their way; and the sun went down on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.

paite: Gibeah a giak ding in alut ua, alut un huai khopi kholak ah atu uh; kuamah zintun ding a-om ngal kei ua.
english: They went over there, to go in to stay in Gibeah. He went in, and sat down in the street of the city; for there was no one who took them into his house to stay.

paite: Ngai in, nitaklam in putek khat lou kuan ahong pai hi. Huai mi bel Ephraim tanggam a mi ahi a, Gibeah a om zual ahi. Amah Benjamin chite lak a ahi.
english: Behold, an old man came from his work out of the field at evening. Now the man was from the hill country of Ephraim, and he lived in Gibeah; but the men of the place were Benjamites.

paite: Akiheileh kholak a mikhualpa amu hi. Putek in, "Koi a hoh ding? Koi a pan a hong pai na hia?" achi hi.
english: He lifted up his eyes, and saw the wayfaring man in the street of the city; and the old man said, “Where are you going? Where did you come from?”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Judah gam a Bethlehem a pan Ephraim tang tawp gam lam a hoh tum ka hi uh. Huai a om ka hi, Bethlehem, Judah gam ah ka va hoh a; tu in TOUPA' inn a hoh tum ka hi. Kuamah hon zintun a-om kei hi.
english: He said to him, “We are passing from Bethlehem Judah to the farther side of the hill country of Ephraim. I am from there, and I went to Bethlehem Judah. I am going to Yahweh’s house; and there is no one who has taken me into his house.

paite: Ka sabiltung ua ding buhpawl leh gan an ka nei uh. Kei leh na sikhanu leh na sikhate kiang a om tangval a ding leng tanghou leh uain a-om lai a, bangmah taksap ka nei kei uh," achi hi.
english: Yet there is both straw and feed for our donkeys; and there is bread and wine also for me, and for your servant, and for the young man who is with your servants. There is no lack of anything.”

paite: Putek in, "Lungmuangtak in om in. Na kulna tengteng ke'n ka tum vek ding. Kholak ah zaw giak mahmah ke'n," achi hi.
english: The old man said, “Peace be to you! Just let me supply all your needs, but don’t sleep in the street.”

paite: Huchi in a-inn ah apilut a, sabiltungte an apia a; akhete uh asil ua, ne in adawn uhi.
english: So he brought him into his house, and gave the donkeys fodder. Then they washed their feet, and ate and drank.

paite: Huchi a nuamsa leh kipaktak a a-om lai un, ngai in, huai khua a mi, Belial tapate khenkhat in huai inn ahon umta uh. Kongkhak ahong khen ua; inn neipa putek kiang ah, "Na inn a hong tungpa hon pikhia in, ka kithuahpih ding uh," achi uhi.
english: As they were making their hearts merry, behold, the men of the city, certain wicked fellows, surrounded the house, beating at the door; and they spoke to the master of the house, the old man, saying, “Bring out the man who came into your house, that we can have sex with him!”

paite: Inn neipa akiang uah ava pawt a, akiang uah, "Hilou e, ka unaute aw, hichi tel a gilou zaw hih mahmah kei un. Hiai mi ka mikhual ahi. Hiai thil haihuai hih kei un," achi hi.
english: The man, the master of the house, went out to them, and said to them, “No, my brothers, please don’t act so wickedly; since this man has come into my house, don’t do this folly.

paite: "Ngai un, hiai ah ka tanu nungak leh amei a-om uh. Amau ka hon pikhe dia, amaute zahlaksak in na ut-ut uh atung uah hih un. Himahleh hiai mi tung ah zaw hiai thil gilou hih kei un," achi hi.
english: Behold, here is my virgin daughter and his concubine. I will bring them out now. Humble them, and do with them what seems good to you; but to this man don’t do any such folly.”

paite: Himahleh huai mite'n athu azui nuam kei ua, huchi in hiai mi'n amei aman a, akiang uah ava pikhia hi. Amau ana kithuahpih ua, khovak masiah zankhua in apawngsual uhi. Huchi a khua ahong vaktak in, akhah uhi.
english: But the men wouldn’t listen to him; so the man grabbed his concubine, and brought her out to them; and they had sex with her, and abused her all night until the morning. When the day began to dawn, they let her go.

paite: Khua ahong vaktak in numei apai a, apu tunnapa inn kongpi bul ah apuk a, khovak nung tan in a-om nilouh hi.
english: Then the woman came in the dawning of the day, and fell down at the door of the man’s house where her lord was, until it was light.

paite: Apu zingsang in ahong thou a, inn kongpite ahong a, pai tum in ava pawt hi. Ngai in, ameinu kongpi bul ah akhutte insung lam nga in ana lum hi.
english: Her lord rose up in the morning and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way; and behold, the woman his concubine had fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands on the threshold.

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Thou in, i pai ding,” achi hi. Himahleh adawng kei. Huchi in asabiltung tung ah akoihtou a; athou a, amun lam ah apaita hi.
english: He said to her, “Get up, and let’s get going!” but no one answered. Then he took her up on the donkey; and the man rose up, and went to his place.

paite: A-inn atun in temta ala a, amei asem a, aguhte toh seh sawm-le-nih in asemnen a, Israel gam teng ah akhak vek hi.
english: When he had come into his house, he took a knife and cut up his concubine, and divided her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the borders of Israel.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, amu peuhmahte'n, "Israel suante Aigupta gam a pan ahong pawt nung uh hichibang thilhih leh muh tutan in a-om ngei nai kei. 'Ngaihtuah unla, kihou unla, na lungsim uh gen un, " achi uhi.
english: It was so, that all who saw it said, “Such a deed has not been done or seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt to this day! Consider it, take counsel, and speak.”
